chapter: Philadelphia and the McRae Brothers Band, 1908-1929
title: E-flat soprano, Coon-Sanders, and Rollini as bass sax inspiration
summary: McRae recalls hearing an E-flat soprano in Detroit with Chick, and Adrian Rollini's bass sax with Coon-Sanders as his inspiration.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

blocks.x: Right today, I haven't seen a band yet that played (inaudible). I ran across a band in

S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC.
WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Detroit when we're playing with Chick. The guy had an E-flat soprano. And it's beautiful. It's a wonderful saxophone, but nobody played it.
Had played it once in a while.
When we were in Atlantic City, Coon-Sanders was there -- the band from out west.
Yeah, the Black Hawks. Now the fellow that played bass sax -- I forget his name, he's very popular.
I got my inspiration from him from playing bass saxophone. They did a thing called
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
"Stomping the Dog and Kicking The Cat." And this was something that the bass saxophone played. They featured a bass saxophone on this. And I got one.
Then Coleman Hawkins with Fletcher back in those days -- and Coleman played bass. Coleman was a great bass saxophone player! I think he was just as good as Rollini or any of the guys.
When I came to New York, I said I got to hear Coleman play that bass saxophone.
